cards.text: Jesus has been staying across the Jordan, after a crowd in Jerusalem tried to seize Him (John 10:39-40). Meanwhile, a man named Lazarus is sick, back home in the village of his sisters, Mary and Martha. This is the same Mary who will one day anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.

cards.question: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, is sick. Which village does he live in?

cards.text: So the sisters send word to Jesus: "Lord, the one You love is sick." Short and clear, friend, which is more than I can say for MY texts, which run three paragraphs and STILL forget the point.

cards.question: When Jesus hears that Lazarus is sick, He says this sickness will end in death.
Jesus says Lazarus's sickness is for something, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it. What is it for?

answers.text: A test of the sisters' faith

cards.text: Then the story stops to make one thing clear: Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

cards.question: When Jesus hears Lazarus is sick, He sets out for Bethany right away.
Instead of leaving for Bethany, Jesus stays where He is for ___ days.

cards.text: Then He says to the disciples, "Let us go back to Judea." That's the same area as Jerusalem, where that crowd just tried to seize Him.

cards.question: The disciples call Jesus Rabbi and push back on going to Judea. What do they remind Him?

answers.text: The Jews just tried to stone Him
The sisters told Him to stay away

cards.text: The disciples are NOT excited about Judea, and I get it. My oven singed my mustache ONE time, and to this day I open it from across the room.
The disciples just reminded Jesus about the stones. He answers with a question: "Are there not twelve hours of daylight?"

cards.question: Jesus goes on: whoever walks in the ___ won't stumble, because he sees by the light of this world. But whoever walks at ___ will stumble.

cards.text: After He says this, Jesus tells them their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep.

cards.question: Jesus says their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. What does He say He's going to do?

answers.text: Go there and wake him up
Let him rest a while longer
Pray for him from right here

cards.question: The disciples reply that if Lazarus is sleeping, he will get better.
The disciples thought Jesus meant actual sleep. What was He really talking about?

cards.text: So Jesus tells them plainly: Lazarus is dead.

cards.question: Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there when Lazarus died. Whose sake does He say that's for?
Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there, so that the disciples may believe.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "But let us go to him." And Thomas, one of the disciples, also called Didymus, turns to the others.

cards.question: Judea is where they just tried to stone Jesus. What does Thomas tell his fellow disciples?

answers.text: Let us also go so that we may die with Him
Let us stay here until it is safe to travel
Let us send word to the sisters before we go

cards.text: That's not exactly a pep talk, but Thomas is IN. Me? It took an ANGEL to get me out of a junk drawer.
And that's where we'll pause. Hold onto your apron, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The question already says the sickness is 'so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.' That points straight to 'The glory of God' and rules out the two wrong answers, so the baker doesn't need to reason anything out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says Judea is 'the same area as Jerusalem, where that crowd just tried to seize Him.' Both facts come from outside the passage (Jerusalem: John 10:22-23; the attempt to seize Him: John 10:39), but the card gives no reference, and its citation covers only John 11:7.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card calls the people who tried to seize Jesus 'a crowd in Jerusalem,' and stop 1 card 9 repeats 'that crowd.' John 10:31-39 calls them 'the Jews' and never calls them a crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card only restates that the disciples don't want to go to Judea, which card 10 already covered, and then adds the oven joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card retells John 11:8 ('The disciples just reminded Jesus about the stones') but cites only John 11:9.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answers stand out. 'Twelve hours of daylight' and 'the light of this world' point straight to 'daytime.' For the second blank, 'night' is the only word that fits 'walks at ___.' 'At city,' 'at wilderness' and 'at crowd' don't read as real choices.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. Thomas chooses to walk toward danger with Jesus. Papa Dorin being called out of a junk drawer was a rescue, not going toward danger, so the comparison doesn't click. The card also adds nothing new from the passage after card 11.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to Thomas's line, which card 11 already asked. It doesn't tell any part of the passage, so it is a joke-only card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
